articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Atlético de Madrid vs Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: William Hill te ofrece el pronóstico del derbi madrileño correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: William Hill te ofrece el pronóstico del derbi madrileño correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Atlético de Madrid recibe al Real Madrid este domingo en el Riyadh Air Metropolitano, en el derbi madrileño correspondiente a la séptima jornada de LaLiga 26/27. El conjunto de Diego Simeone llega a este compromiso con la necesidad de reaccionar tras un tramo irregular. Cayó por un contundente 3-0 ante el Athletic Club en San Mamés, un correctivo que dejó serias dudas sobre el rendimiento colchonero fuera de casa, pero ganó 4-0 a Osasuna en su último duelo. Favorito para el partido entre Atlético de Madrid y Real Madrid Por su parte, el Real Madrid llega al derbi con pleno de confianza tras sufrir de más de lo esperado en su última salida liguera. El conjunto de José Mourinho se impuso por 2-3 al Elche en el Martínez Valero, en un partido en el que llegó a ir 0-2 arriba, se dejó remontar y necesitó un gol de Carlos Espí en el descuento para llevarse los tres puntos, resultado que le permite alcanzar los 15 puntos y meter presión al líder Barcelona antes de este exigente desplazamiento al Metropolitano. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como favorito al Real Madrid, aunque sin una diferencia demasiado amplia dado que se trata de un derbi. William Hill paga la victoria visitante a cuota 1.95, por 3.60 del empate y 3.50 de la victoria del cuadro colchonero. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Atlético ha encajado goles con demasiada facilidad en sus últimas dos salidas, sumando cinco tantos en contra entre Liga y Champions, mientras que el Real Madrid tampoco ha logrado mantener su portería a cero en su última salida, encajando dos goles ante el Elche pese a la victoria final. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Bet365 paga a 1.44 el "sí" y a 2.62 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con bastante producción ofensiva. El Real Madrid ha marcado cinco goles en sus dos últimos partidos, mientras que el Atlético, pese a sus dificultades defensivas, también ha demostrado capacidad para ver puerta en la mayoría de sus salidas. Con estos datos, William Hill sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.44, por 2.7 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Real Madrid, con su juego de posesión y dominio territorial marcado por Mourinho, suele generar un volumen alto de saques de esquina en sus desplazamientos, especialmente ante rivales que sufren para contener su ataque. El Atlético, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus últimas salidas un perfil más replegado tras los golpes sufridos ante Athletic y Liverpool, lo que invita a pensar en una diferencia de córners favorable al conjunto blanco en este derbi.

articles.title: Atlético Nacional terminaría su contrato con Nike a finales de 2026: qué marca lo vestiría
articles.standfirst: Atlético Nacional le pondría fin a su relación con Nike tras 13 años y apostaría por una marca propia para 2027
articles.summary: Atlético Nacional le pondría fin a su relación con Nike tras 13 años y apostaría por una marca propia para 2027
articles.body: Un giro trascendental sacude la estructura comercial e institucional de Atlético Nacional. Luego de más de una década vistiendo el reconocido Swoosh de la multinacional estadounidense Nike, la institución 'Verdolaga' ha tomado la decisión de dar un paso al costado y no renovar su contrato a finales de 2026. En lugar de migrar a otra gran firma deportiva del mercado internacional, el conjunto antioqueño apostará por un modelo de negocio innovador en el país: la creación de su propia marca de indumentaria deportiva a partir de 2027. La alianza entre Atlético Nacional y Nike comenzó en el año 2013, marcando un hito para el fútbol profesional colombiano al consolidar al equipo paisa como uno de los referentes indiscutibles del continente. A lo largo de estos 13 años, el club vistió la indumentaria de la firma estadounidense en algunas de sus gestas deportivas más memorables, destacando la consecución de múltiples títulos de la Liga BetPlay, Copas Colombia y la histórica Copa Libertadores de América en 2016. Sin embargo, a pesar del éxito comercial y deportivo acumulado durante más de un decenio, las diferencias estratégicas y contractuales entre ambas partes precipitaron la decisión de no extender la relación laboral una vez venza el contrato vigente en diciembre de 2026. Según lo dio a conocer en exclusiva el periodista deportivo Juan David Londoño, Atlético Nacional no contempla negociar un nuevo patrocinio técnico con competidores tradicionales del sector como Adidas, Puma, New Balance o Reebok. La dirigencia 'Verdolaga' proyecta desarrollar su propia línea interna de diseño, fabricación y distribución. "Confirmado: Atlético Nacional tendrá su marca propia para la camiseta de competencia e indumentaria en general a partir de 2027. Por varias diferencias, el contrato con Nike terminará en diciembre", detalló el comunicador. Los ejes del nuevo modelo: Esta transformación corporativa coincide con un momento de enorme impacto mediático y deportivo para Atlético Nacional. Recientemente, el club ratificó su protagonismo en la Liga BetPlay tras vencer 2-3 a Internacional de Bogotá en el estadio El Campín, un compromiso que contó además con el debut oficial del volante James Rodríguez vistiendo la camiseta 'Verdolaga'. El cambio hacia una marca propia representa una apuesta audaz en la industria del fútbol colombiano, con la que Atlético Nacional no solo busca refrescar su imagen estética para la temporada 2027, sino también fortalecer su modelo financiero de cara al futuro.

articles.title: Bordalás: “La jugada del gol es cuanto menos muy dudosa, Isco le tapa la visibilidad a David Soria”
articles.standfirst: El técnico azulón destacó el trabajo de los suyos ante un gran rival
articles.body: El Getafe cayó este jueves en La Cartuja frente al Real Betis en un encuentro tras el que Bordalás destaca el “esfuerzo” de sus jugadores. El alicantino señaló que su equipo estuvo “serio” y destacó que en el feudo verdiblanco “ha competido” frente a un equipo con una “plantilla espectacular”. Valoración: “El equipo se va triste puesto que hemos perdido. Felicitar a los chicos, han hecho un esfuerzo muy grande, han competido dentro de nuestras posibilidades. Ha sido una pena frente a un equipo como el Betis, que tiene una plantilla espectacular. El equipo ha estado serio, ha competido. Triste por los chicos. Ya hay que corregir lo que hayamos podido hacer mal y esté en nuestra mano. Ha habido detalles que nos han penalizado, sobre todo el gol que es cuanto menos extraño, está Isco delante de Soria. No tiene visibilidad y la regla dice que cuando se obstaculiza la visión se tiene que anular”. Qué ha faltado: “Nos enfrentamos a un rival en un momento increíble, con un plantel enorme, sabíamos que iba a ser difícil. Estábamos serios, sabíamos que iba a ser difícil y ha llegado esa jugada del gol que cuanto menos es muy dudosa. Estaba Isco ahí, estiró la pierna y le tapó la visibilidad a David Soria”. Mano de Abde en el gol: “Sí, la tenía pegada, pero se ayuda para amortiguar el balón. Esas acciones suelen ser mano, pero al margen de eso me quedo con el esfuerzo del equipo. Tenemos que seguir mejorando y corregir las cosas que dependen de nosotros”. Roja a Mario: “Está claro que quita la pierna en el último momento. Es impetuoso pero sin maldad. Se ve claramente en la imagen que encoge la pierna. Tenemos que corregir”. Málaga: “Ahora hay que pensar en el próximo compromiso, recuperar a los chicos, no se les puede reprochar nada porque a pesar de las dificultades los chavales lo han dado absolutamente todo. Algunos ya no podían. Nada que reprochar, a pensar en el siguiente compromiso”. Rotaciones: “Venimos desde el inicio jugando los mismos, hoy hemos tenido que dar descanso a algunos. Había compañeros que tenían dificultades en el primer tiempo. Incluso en dar entrada a chicos del filial. Estamos muy justos, ahora hay que recuperarse, pero para nosotros es una dificultad máxima jugar tres partidos entre semana”.

articles.title: La Juve enmienda el 'borrón'
articles.standfirst: Los goles de Nico González, Alajbegovic y Woltemade antes del descanso aclararon la goleada ante un débil NEC Nimega (5-0) · Kolo Muani se reivindicó marcando y asistiendo
articles.summary: Los goles de Nico González, Alajbegovic y Woltemade antes del descanso aclararon la goleada ante un débil NEC Nimega (5-0) · Kolo Muani se reivindicó marcando y asistiendo
articles.body: La derrota de la Juventus frente al Sassuolo en Serie A el pasado fin de semana dejó el proyecto de Spalletti en una posición comprometida. Venían avisados del asalto a San Siro por parte del Benfica un día atrás. Sin embargo, no dieron opción alguna a un débil NEC Nimega (5-0) que se marchó de Turín con una 'manita'. Lo en el Mapei Stadium tuvo sus consecuencias en el once presentado por la Juventus: Grabara relevó a Vicario bajo palos; Pape Sarr entró en el doble pivote; y Woltemade dejó en el banquillo a un Kolo Muani cuyo rendimiento en su retorno a la Juventus, ya en propiedad, está levantando críticas. Los cambios introducidos por Spalletti también trajeron consigo una modificación en el dibujo de una 'Vecchia Signora' que se organizó con una línea de tres centrales. Hubo cierto tanteo inicial por parte de ambos equipos. Pero, a los ocho minutos, Nico González castigó una salida en falso de Polster tras envío largo de Gravara para marcar el 1-0 a placer. Sigue reivindicándose el argentino en su regreso a Turín. Lejos de tratar de aprovechar el impulso del gol, la Juventus optó por adoptar una postura bastante conservadora. No le terminaba de convencer a Spalletti lo que estaba viendo desde la zona técnica... a pesar de que su equipo estaba por delante en el marcador. El NEC, que tampoco estaba teniendo la inspiración que le caracteriza, se seguía mostrando demasiado frágil atrás y, en el 24', Alajbegovic celebró su primer gol como 'bianconero' luciendo golpeo de balón. No le paraban de crecer los enanos al NEC Nimega. Bischoff, uno de sus jugadores más talentosos, tuvo que abandonar el campo en el 32' por lesión y, sólo un minuto después, de la conexión entre Alajbegovic y Nico González se originó el penalti transformado por Woltemade. Otro que estrenaba su cuenta personal como nuevo jugador de la Juventus. El NEC Nimega trató de hacer 'borrón y cuenta nueva' para afrontar la segunda. Ahora bien, aunque se adueñaron del balón, lo cierto es que no incomodó a una Juventus que se permitió reservar efectivos pensando en el duelo frente a Atalanta. A la hora de partido, Spalletti retiró a McKennie, Douglas Luíz y Nico González. Tampoco tardó demasiado en saltar al césped un Kolo Muani que necesitaba reivindicarse. Primero asistió a Celik tras una buena acción por banda y, posteriormente, marcó su primer gol de la temporada castigando otra deficiente salida de Polster. La Juventus necesitaba despejar dudas y firmó una goleada para cumplir con su etiqueta de 'favorito' en esta Europa League.

articles.title: La Real paga con una derrota su pésimo inicio
articles.standfirst: El conjunto txuriurdin fue muy superado por el Bournemouth en la primera parte y encajó dos goles que no pudo ni igualar pese a su gran mejoría en la segunda
articles.summary: El conjunto txuriurdin fue muy superado por el Bournemouth en la primera parte y encajó dos goles que no pudo ni igualar pese a su gran mejoría en la segunda
articles.body: La Real Sociedad cayó por 1-2 ante el Bournemouth, en su estreno en la Europa League de esta temporada y lo hizo por su pésima primera parte, en la que fue muy superada y encajó dos goles que pudieron ser más y que no llegó ni a igualar pese a merecerlo por su gran mejoría tras el descanso, debido a la falta de acierto en el final de sus ataques. El Bournemouth salió muy atrevido, presionando arriba a la salida del balón de una Real que jugó por primera vez con cinco defensas, y buscando con rapidez el área de Marrero, con Rayan haciendo el primer remate del partido, al cuerpo de Sergio Gómez. Cuando parecía que los de Matarazzo empezaban a controlar el juego, un maravilloso centro de Truffert terminó con un remate en boca de gol de Kluivert, para adelantar a los visitantes, que en su siguiente aproximación volvieron a repetir un centro desde la izquierda y un remate al segundo palo, en esta ocasión de Rayan, que subió el 0-2 al electrónico de Anoeta, en una acción en la que Marrero pareció medir mal. Los txuriurdin, totalmente superados, respiraron con tranquilidad cuando, prácticamente en la siguiente jugada, Evanilson cabeceó al poste izquierdo de la portería del azpeitiarra. Algunos aficionados, decepcionados, respondieron con silbidos que fueron mayores cuando Antonio Silva volvió a rematar con la testa con gran comodidad, aunque afortunadamente fuera. El descanso era lo mejor que le podía venir a la Real. La salida de los vestuarios, en donde Matarazzo dejó a Fort para dar entrada a Guedes, fue prometedora, con un centro chut muy desviado de Barrenetxea, otra internada del 7 parada con falta y un disparo lejano de Turrientes que hizo que viésemos por primera vez a Petrovic, que metió la manopla para mandar el balón a córner. La reacción tuvo premio, porque en uno de sus golpeos con rosca, medio centro, medio disparo, Sergio Gómez vio como la pelota terminaba en el fondo de la red. El Bournemouth reaccionó bien, con un disparo de Evanilson a las manos de Marrero, pero los txuriurdin querían más y Guedes puso a prueba a Petrovic, al que Oyarzabal intentó superar de vaselina, sin éxito. Óskarsson tuvo el empate, pero se encontró con el guardameta visitante, que luego se alivió al ver irse fuera un cabezazo de Jon Martín y salvó otra vez el tanto del islandés en un remate a bocajarro, en la última opción para evitar una derrota dolorosa por la pésima primera mitad.

articles.title: Analysis: Palace make light work of step up
articles.summary: It has been a memorable couple of years for Palace fans with their stunning FA Cup win two seasons ago followed by European glory in the Conference League....
articles.body:
It has been a memorable couple of years for Palace fans with their stunning FA Cup win two seasons ago followed by European glory in the Conference League.

The Europa League, however, marks a step up in quality and supporters will have been cautiously optimistic about how their team would handle it.

On this showing they will have every reason to believe their side can at least reach the knockout stage, though they were helped out by a Lech Poznan side that did themselves no favours.

Terry Yegbe's throw for Palace's opener was a dreadful error of judgement as he simply gifted the ball to Pino , who gratefully waltzed into the area to score.

They never really recovered from that and only the offside flag spared further blushes when Yegbe launched a bizarre attempted clearance into his own net from about 35 yards.

To their credit, the visiting supporters never gave up chanting throughout the second half, even if they had no goal to celebrate, as instead Palace added a late fourth to round off a win that will give them much-needed confidence after a difficult start to the Premier League season, losing three out of four games.

There was one other significant moment for Palace in the second half as Ismaila Sarr came on for his first appearance of the season.

A proposed move to Liverpool collapsed late in the transfer window, and while his return to action was generally well received, there were some boos among the cheers.

articles.title: 6 best and worst fantasy football matchups for Week 2
articles.summary: Three players have great Week 2 fantasy football matchups, while three others may need to remain on your bench. Where does Jordan Love land?
articles.body:
We're onto Week 2, and there was a lot of new fantasy football information to take in after a record-setting Week 1 slate that saw half of the teams in the NFL reach 26 points (seriously).

It's worth mentioning, like last week, that matchups analysis like mine will only become more accurate as the season moves along. The Chicago Bears aren't going to score 59 points each week, the Chargers are not going to finish the season winless and Kenneth Walker is not going to finish the season with nearly 3,000 rushing yards.

That said, there was a lot to learn from Week 1, and I've identified six key matchups to know for our second saga of the season.

Note: Projections refer to player props in the betting and prediction markets, which are a valuable reference tool for anyone playing fantasy football.

Notable injuries throughout the 2026 NFL season

The Jets defense performed well in Week 1 despite a real lack of talent on that side of the ball. However, that was against a Titans offense that will hover near the bottom across every major offensive category all season. Tennessee 's offensive line in particular is quite possibly the league's worst.

Yet, Titans QB Cam Ward was only pressured on 31% of his pass attempts in Week 1. Love, on the other hand, was constantly under fire against the Vikings , with a staggering 45% of his pass attempts coming under pressure (in typical Brian Flores fashion).

In a clean pocket, Love averaged an outrageous 9.9 yards per pass attempt and threw two touchdowns. Love should have much more favorable conditions in this matchup, and his passing yards prop of 257.5 yards is rightfully the third-highest of Week 2. Combined with the Packers ' disappointing run game, Green Bay is going to dial up the volume for Love to get the first win of 2026.

The Vikings employed a committee approach at running back in Week 1, but that's about to change in Week 2 now that Jordan Mason is headed to IR due to thumb surgery .

Aaron Jones is 31 years old and no longer an elite runner of the football like he once was. But, he's still a more than competent pass-catcher. The Bears allowed the Panthers backs to pile up 86 receiving yards last week, and Chicago also enters this matchup as 4.5-point home favorites.

QB Carson Wentz 's mobility is far more limited than Kyler Murray , so we should see ample check-downs to Jones anytime he's under pressure. And, with the Vikings expected to trail, Jones now has pass-catching momentum from two angles. Jones' 81.5 total yards prop is actually *higher* than D'Andre Swift's this week, another indication that Jones is a locked-in fantasy starter in the right matchup for his skill set.

Technically, I could have written up any 49ers player against a Dolphins defense that just allowed a Brock Bowers-less Raiders team to put up 27 points.

We're going with Mike Evans to get back at "Big Fantasy" for telling you that Evans has a *tough* matchup this week. Every fantasy football platform is marking Evans' matchup with red ink, because yes, the Dolphins limited the Raiders ' wide receivers last week. But, there's a big difference between Evans and the motley collection of Tre Tucker , Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech .

No Raiders receiver reached 30 yards against the Dolphins' inexperienced cornerback trio, and that will change with Evans this week. Throughout this game, Evans will match up with a 5th round pick from last year or a journeyman corner with 19 career games played, all while having a several inch height advantage along with a 30-40 pound weight advantage.

After being targeted on nearly 1 in 3 routes in his 49ers debut, expect Evans to be a force coming off 10 days rest.

The Jaguars QB just shredded a hapless Browns defense for 245 yards and four touchdowns, but this matchup is significantly more challenging.

Yes, the Broncos put up a historically bad tackling performance on prime time Monday Night Football against the Chiefs. However, the Broncos still have a filthy defense on paper, and one game against Patrick Mahomes shouldn't radically change how we view this unit overall.

Vegas is giving significant respect to the Broncos' defense, as Lawrence's pass yards prop is just 222 yards, and his pass touchdowns line of 1.5 is heavily shaded towards the under. In this same game, Bo Nix has better passing projections.

The Jaguars have a well below average offensive line, and the Broncos' pass rush should be able to exploit this. Think of Lawrence as just outside the fantasy QB1 radar in this matchup.

The Rams played in Australia without Aaron Donald , and essentially without Myles Garrett , who underwent knee surgery immediately following that game. Donald is expected back for Week 2, and the entire Rams defense is getting 11 days of rest for this contest.

The Giants moved the ball at will against Dallas in Week 1, controlling time of possession. This week, the Rams are 7-point favorites, which naturally does not bode well for New York's rushing expectations. Skattebo's rush yards prop is among the lowest at the position this week (50.5 yards), and his touchdown odds are below 50%.

Skattebo is nothing more than a flex play in a bounce-back spot for the Rams.

The Eagles corners are incredible, and they just held Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs to a combined six receptions for 69 yards. This was amplified by the Eagles' ferocious pass rush and the Commanders ' porous offensive line.

This week, we get the more extreme version of this matchup mismatch, as the Titans have the actual worst offensive line in the NFL. Carnell Tate was targeted nearly three times further downfield than teammate Wan'Dale Robinson in Week 1.

Cam Ward will be relentlessly pressured like Jayden Daniels last week. Daniels, who was pressured on nearly 50% of his pass attempts, averaged just 1.7 yards per attempt in those scenarios. The Titans' team total is just 16 points, and Tate's receiving yard line is only 40 in the prop markets.

It will be a Herculean feat to get Tate the ball downfield in this matchup, and he should be parked on your fantasy bench in Week 2.

articles.title: The NFL Fantasy Hobby Waiver Wire: Week 1
articles.summary: Welcome back to the first official regular-season edition of The Hobby Waiver Wire Year 2! If you followed along last year, you know the drill: we are target...
articles.body:
Welcome back to the first official regular-season edition of The Hobby Waiver Wire Year 2! If you followed along last year, you know the drill: we are targeting players to collect and invest in based strictly on their on-field fantasy football performance. Gut feelings and hype trains take a backseat here; we are making data-backed hobby decisions driven by actual usage, targets, and fantasy production.

If you want a baseline for how we approach this, check out last week's breakdown of Silver Prizm PSA 10 prices relative to preseason fantasy rankings . Now that Week 1 is in the books, the market is already reacting. Here is who you need to put a claim in for on the secondary market.

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

Buckle in, K9 fans, you best hop on the Kenneth Walker III train right now. The reigning Super Bowl MVP is not playing around in his new uniform. Walker rushed 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown while bringing in three of his six targets for 18 yards and another score during the Chiefs' 31-10 runaway win over the Broncos on Monday night.

The Card: 2022 Panini Prizm Silver #318 (PSA 10)

The Verdict: His flagship Prizm Silver PSA 10 was sitting around $80 to $90 just last week. After one game in the Kansas City offense, it's selling for $200. If he can maintain even a fraction of this Week 1 output, his cards will see considerable sustained growth this season. With other unproven, younger running backs like Ashton Jeanty already selling for $200-plus, K9 looks like a value. If you can snipe a PSA 10 Silver Rookie of his for under $150 on an auction, it is an absolute snap buy.

Watson put together an absolutely electric game despite the final score. He caught six of his eight targets for 147 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 39-22 loss to the Vikings, proving that when he is healthy, he is a premier deep threat with slate-breaking fantasy upside.

The Card: 2022 Panini Prizm Silver (PSA 10)

The Verdict: His PSA 10 Silver Prizm Rookies aren't incredibly easy to find right now, the pop count is sitting at only 38, but they were quietly selling between $40 and $70 during the preseason. With a performance like this, it would not be surprising to see his cards surge into the $150 territory if he continues this pace of play. If you can get one for under $100 right now, it represents a very smart buy.

Olave commanded massive volume in Week 1, catching 10 of his 13 targets for 182 yards in Sunday's 31-30 overtime loss to the Lions. He looks to be the unquestioned number-one option for a quarterback who absolutely loves to chuck the ball down the field. Volume is king in fantasy football, and Olave is clearly getting the lion's share.

The Verdict: His Rookie Silver Prizm PSA 10 has been sitting at a very affordable $70, which is wild considering it boasts a pop count under 10. Because of how scarce the gem-mint Silvers currently are, if you think Olave is your man this season, it is highly recommended to venture into his other Prizm color parallels . Or check your boxes at home for Silver rookies to grade. There are plenty of low-numbered PSA 10s out there that remain incredibly affordable.

Why are this man's cards so remarkably cheap? Hurts was efficient enough in Sunday's 24-22 win against the Commanders, completing 14 of 25 pass attempts for 203 yards, three passing touchdowns, and zero interceptions. Add in his usual rushing floor, seven carries for 46 yards, and he remains one of the safest elite assets in the league.

The Card: 2020 Panini Prizm Silver #343 (PSA 10)

The Verdict: His Rookie Prizm Silver PSA 10 currently sells for less than $600. Let that sink in. That is $400 cheaper than Trevor Lawrence and Drake Maye , and about $150 to $200 less than unproven commodities like Bo Nix and Jaxson Dart. The hobby loves chasing the shiny new toy, but buying an established, MVP-caliber quarterback at a massive discount compared to rookies who haven't accomplished anything in the league is a glaring market inefficiency you should exploit.

Early-season market swings move fast, and capitalizing on early volume before the rest of the hobby catches on is how you stay ahead of the curve. Whether you're snatching up an MVP-caliber quarterback at a discount or riding the early breakout momentum of high-usage playmakers, making data-backed moves beats relying on pure gut feeling every single time.

Check back next week after the Week 2 games wrap up to see who made the cut on the next edition of The Hobby Waiver Wire!

articles.title: Gabriel Milito, Unbeaten Against América
articles.summary: El Clásico de México is just around the corner, and ahead of another edition of this rivalry in Matchday 9 of the Apertura 2026, Guadalajara has an important...
articles.body:
El Clásico de México is just around the corner, and ahead of another edition of this rivalry in Matchday 9 of the Apertura 2026, Guadalajara has an important precedent on its side: Gabriel Milito remains unbeaten against América since taking charge of the Rebaño Sagrado.

The Argentine manager has coached 2 Clásicos de México in Liga MX, and both ended in Rojiblanco victories. The first came in Matchday 8 of the Apertura 2025, when Chivas visited the Azulcrema side in Mexico City and won 1-2 with goals from Roberto Alvarado and Armando González .

That night, Guadalajara showed the personality to go toe-to-toe with its opponent on their home turf and found the goals in the second half that allowed them to claim a statement victory. Alvarado opened the scoring and, near the end, Armando González appeared to extend the lead and cap off a special night for the Rebaño.

The story repeated itself in the Clausura 2026. In Matchday 6, Estadio AKRON witnessed another Rojiblanco victory, this time by a 1-0 scoreline. Armando González once again took center stage, scoring the only goal of the match and giving Chivas another win over América.

In between those 2 official meetings, there was also a friendly Clásico in the United States, which ended 1-1 with a goal from Javier ' Chicharito ' Hernández for Guadalajara. As a result, Milito has yet to taste defeat against América since taking over the Rojiblanco bench.

A Team That Knows How to Play in Clásicos

The precedent is not only backed by the results. In their 2 Liga MX matches, Chivas has shown the ability to compete against América in different aspects of the game: with organization, initiative, personality on the ball and determination in key moments.

Guadalajara has known how to approach these types of matches under Milito. In the first, they prevailed away from home; in the second, they defended their home turf and found the difference in a tight match. Two different scenarios, the same outcome: a Rojiblanco victory.

Now, the challenge will once again take place in the nation's capital. Chivas will visit América this Saturday, September 19, in Matchday 9 of the Apertura 2026, looking to extend their good run and, in the process, maintain Milito's positive streak against their fiercest rival.

The Rebaño Sagrado will arrive at El Clásico de México sitting in second place with 17 points and a run of 7 consecutive Liga MX matches without a defeat, recording 5 wins and 2 draws. In addition, the Tapatío side has gone 191 minutes without conceding a goal, making it the best defense in the tournament with just 6 goals allowed. On the other side, América sits third in the standings with 16 points.

The stage is set for another chapter in this rivalry. Gabriel Milito already knows what it means to beat América away from home and to do it at Estadio AKRON . Now he will face another test, once again in the nation's capital and against a team that is also battling near the top of the table.

2 Clásicos de México coached in Liga MX, 2 wins for Chivas. This Saturday, Guadalajara will look to write another chapter in a streak that remains intact so far.

articles.title: Ole Miss bans LSU football fans from student section for Lane Kiffin's return
articles.summary: Ole Miss announced in an email sent to students that fans supporting LSU would not be allowed into the student section for Lane Kiffin's return.
articles.body:
OXFORD — Ole Miss athletics announced in an email sent to students Sept. 17 that fans supporting LSU would not be allowed into the student section for Lane Kiffin 's return in Week 3.

"Effective immediately, no person wearing an opposing team's gear or colors will be allowed entrance into the student section," the email said. "Additionally, anyone found to be wearing opposing team apparel or colors in the student section will be removed."

The No. 9 Rebels (2-0) are hosting the No. 7 Tigers (2-0) on Sept. 19 (6:30 p.m., ABC) at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. The drama around the matchup is expected to create a memorable environment. Kiffin, LSU's coach who left Ole Miss before the College Football Playoff in 2025, is public enemy No. 1 in Oxford .

What happened between Ole Miss, LSU fans

There is some recent history involving Ole Miss and LSU fans.

Lane Kiffin, LSU football coach returning to Ole Miss for Week 3 game

A video surfaced of an incident during an Ole Miss vs LSU baseball game April 11 at Swayze Field that involved an LSU fan in the bleachers in right field, which is a general admission section where Ole Miss students sit.

A man wearing a bright yellow LSU jersey and purple LSU hat was being led out of the section. A drink was sprayed at him as he had his back turned.

As a security guard tried to get between the LSU fan and where the drink was thrown, the LSU fan charged in and punched a man with his left hand. He punched him on the ground before the scuffle was broken up.

What fans can expect at Ole Miss-LSU football game

ESPN's "College GameDay" will feature the Ole Miss-LSU football game with guest picker Morgan Freeman . There are some additions to the game atmosphere that Drew Ingraham, Ole Miss' Senior Associate AD for External Engagement, and his team have worked to create.

There will be two flyovers. Two C-17 planes, large military transport aircraft, will pass over Vaught-Hemingway during the national anthem. There will also be a flyover at 8 a.m. for "College GameDay." That will be done by two military helicopters.

There will be two drone shows at the game as well. Ole Miss is has introduced a "Code Powder" segment this season between the first quarter and the second quarter. It's reminiscent of the "Code Red" light show Ole Miss holds between the third and fourth quarters.

A drone show will accompany both periods. Ole Miss is partnering with SkyWorx for the show.

Fans will also be provided with flashing wristbands. It's something the Rebels did for the 2025 College Football Playoff game vs Tulane — the first game after Kiffin left — and got rave reviews.

Between the bracelets, flyovers and drone shows, Ingraham said this game hits a trifecta. The fireworks will also be enhanced.

"Obviously team success plays a huge role in all of this," Ingraham said. "Our goal is just to support that. It's to provide additional in-game enjoyment that is in support of team performance and team success."

"College GameDay" will last from 8-11 a.m. in The Grove. The Walk of Champions is scheduled for 4:15 p.m. Gates open at 4:30 p.m. and the national anthem is at 6:25 p.m.

"I think the one thing that we are trying to message to folks is give yourself some extra time and arrive early," Ingraham said. "This is what seems is going to be an all-day affair with GameDay starting at 8 and going to 11, and then you know we just don't anticipate too many folks leaving campus after that."

Sam Hutchens covers Ole Miss for the Clarion Ledger. Email him at Shutchens@gannett.com or reach him on X at @Sam_Hutchens_

articles.title: Photo: José Mourinho’s head-turning new addition to Real Madrid’s training ground
articles.summary: Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho was the mastermind behind a major new addition to the training base in Spain’s capital this week.The installation in que...
articles.body:
Real Madrid head coach José Mourinho was the mastermind behind a major new addition to the training base in Spain's capital this week.

The installation in question comes in the form of a massive screen. It is expected to be made use of for tactical discussions, as well as watching back over footage of previous outings for specific lessons, with a view to tweaking efforts on and off the ball alike.

A photo of the screen is showcased courtesy of 'Madrid Xtra' on 'X' below:

Mourinho's new-look setup at Valdebebas comes just days out from arguably his side's most high-profile fixture of the new season to date.

On Sunday, Real Madrid are primed to make the short trip across Spain's capital, to lock horns with city rivals Atlético in the campaign's first edition of the Madrid Derby.

Los Merengues head into the matchup boasting a record of six wins from seven across all competitions, but will face an Atléti outfit brimming with confidence after back-to-back victories featuring seven goals scored and none conceded.

articles.title: Cavan Sullivan enters USMNT spotlight with historic potential
articles.summary: By Charles BoehmCould Cavan Sullivan – or Julian Hall, or Justin Ellis, or any of the other young MLS starlets just called into the US men’s national team’s...
articles.body:
Could Cavan Sullivan – or Julian Hall , or Justin Ellis , or any of the other young MLS starlets just called into the US men's national team 's upcoming camp – sooner or later blossom into the United States' equivalent of Spanish teenage sensation Lamine Yamal ?

It's a heady concept. And just the sort of vision Mauricio Pochettino wants to cultivate as he and his staff face the 2030 FIFA World Cup cycle with a big batch of fresh talent in tow.

"From now, if these guys are here and perform in the way that we expect, they are going to have the opportunity, maybe, to play," Pochettino told reporters after releasing a roster packed with new faces on Thursday.

"I don't know. If you see Lamine Yamal, who with Spain won the World Cup [at] 18 years old, but it's now already two years or more than three years that he is playing in Barcelona , and you say, 'no, but he's young, we need more experience.' Why? He is the best.

"If some players that have the same age – 17, 16, 18, 19 – are good, and we are performing and perform well, why we are going [to say,] 'Oh, we need to bring [veterans]'? I think that is an open system … it is about opportunity: Give the opportunity and take the opportunity."

MLS fans familiar with the "Play Your Kids" mantra increasingly common around the league will recognize the framework here. The 28-player group which will gather at U.S. Soccer's new Arthur M. Blank National Training Center in exurban Atlanta next week is more than four years younger on average than the Yanks' 2026 World Cup squad. Its 13 uncapped newcomers are even greener, with an average age of just 19.5.

Sullivan is the youngest among them, and in the eyes of many, holds the most potential. The Philadelphia Union homegrown has been one of MLS's top performers since the World Cup break, with productivity levels matching those of Lionel Messi as Philly stormed from the bottom of the Eastern Conference table to Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs places via an 8W-0L-2D unbeaten run.

"He deserves all the praise that he's getting," said Pochettino of Sullivan, whose club sends more players to this camp than any other. "He's playing well, he's giving assists, scoring goals, and he's 16 – 16. He deserves all the praise. The important thing is to try to help – not to help, but yes, to be with him and to try to provide a solid pattern and support… He deserved to show us in the national team the possibility to talk, the possibility to share ideas, to listen to him, to understand how he is. He is special.

"He deserves to be with us. And this will be a great opportunity for us to know him."

Conversely, Christian Pulisic was left out of this camp after injuries slowed his start to AC Milan 's campaign. Pochettino was uninterested in providing any further details about the star attacker's status, even as he revealed that Folarin Balogun , another regular starter, had been nursing a minor leg injury that was a factor in the USMNT 's evaluations.

That still leaves 13 holdovers from this summer's run to the World Cup Round of 16.

"The young kids, they are going to show us they have the quality," said the coach, "but also they need to feel the support and the guidance of the players with more experience, and we need the players to show the good examples, to show how to behave.

"... It's a good mix of experience and fresh energy, a new energy."

Poch doesn't intend to dial up the hype machine around these youngsters; in fact, he publicly warned them about the pitfalls of that phenomenon just last week. It's more that he's determined to broadcast the message that everyone has a chance to make his squad, regardless of age or pedigree, as long as they're in strong form.

"It's a new start. Of course, all have the door open, but now it's not 'what I did in the past,'" said Pochettino. "Soccer is about today, and that is in the way that we want to build that process and that cycle.

"That is the mentality that we want to build in this process in these four years. If I come, I need to feel that if I perform, and I give to the team what the team expects from me and the coaches expect from me, I'm going to have a percentage – a high percentage – to come back."

This is FIFA's first expanded international autumn window, running from Monday until Oct. 6, enough space to fit in four friendly matches – the Yanks will host Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada – and more time as a group.

It's roomy enough for Pochettino & Co. to welcome former LAFC manager Steve Cherundolo, the recently-appointed US U-23s head coach who will lead the Olympic team on home soil in two years' time, and incorporate many potential members of that project.

Nearly half of this new USMNT roster are age-eligible for Los Angeles 2028, where Poch wants the home nation to be medal contenders, adding that time with the senior side now will be "very helpful" for them when that tournament rolls aroud.

"The federation has to help a little bit to build that way to arrive to the 2028 Olympic Games," he said, "working very closely with Steve, with the under-23s, with all the youth in the federation, all the instructors, to try to build that experience, to arrive to the Olympic Games with the possibility to have that experience that can provide a gold medal.

"That is the objective of the federation, is the objective of everyone, because [this] country loves the Olympic Games, and we know that it's going to be really important for soccer to be sure that we are going to present a very competitive team."

articles.title: SMU football news: Rhett Lashlee explains importance of Week 3 clash vs. Louisville
articles.summary: Rhett Lashlee is looking forward to how No. 16 SMU gears up for its ranked matchup against No. 23 Louisville ahead of Week 3 this season. Lashlee is going th...
articles.body:
Rhett Lashlee is looking forward to how No. 16 SMU gears up for its ranked matchup against No. 23 Louisville ahead of Week 3 this season.

Lashlee is going through the fifth year of his head coaching career with SMU. He has achieved considerable success with the program, leading them to the College Football Playoffs in 2024.

Lashlee appeared on ESPN for an interview in preparation for the Mustangs' contest with Louisville. With both teams firm in the AP Top 25, the coach didn't hold back on the stakes the game has.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"It's a big conference game on the road. I think it's one of two ranked games this week. So it's a huge game, both in the national landscape and in the ACC. For us, we're going on the road for the second time to start the season against a team that is really talented. I mean, these are the last two years we played them. We felt like they were as talented as anybody in the ACC. They're definitely capable of winning the league and making a college football playoff run, and so to have to go into their place and win is a challenge," Lashlee said.

"This game won't define the season for either team, but it could be a launching pad for either one of us. And a lot gets going to get made of the quarterbacks, the offense, all that stuff. At the end of the day, we got two pretty good defenses that maybe aren't getting the credit they deserved. I know their defense is really good. I like our guys; I think it's going to come down to who can run the football, who can stop the run the best, and who can take care of the football."

Lashlee boasts a 40-16 overall record, going 28-5 in the program's conference clashes. Last year saw them go 9-4, ending the campaign with a victory in the Holiday Bowl.

The No. 16 Mustangs will look forward to their next matchup, being on the road. They clash with the No. 23 Louisville Cardinals on Sept. 19 at 3:30 p.m. ET.
